text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; I will need to ask you several questions about your symptoms and medical history to determine the cause. REQUEST TEST: Pulse Oximetry and Arterial Blood Gas.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth at 33 weeks of gestation. Social history: N/A

speaker: Patient
text: The newborn is showing signs of respiratory distress including increased respiratory rate, grunting, and retractions. No other system review was mentioned due to the age of the patient. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That previous suggestion of Tuberculosis is unlikely given the patient's age; newborns do not typically present with active TB in this manner without a long incubation period. While the symptoms of increased respiratory rate, grunting, and retractions are concerning, they are non-specific and require immediate objective data.

REQUEST TEST: Chest X-Ray to evaluate for pneumonia, air leak, or congenital anomalies. REQUEST TEST: Chest Ultrasound to assess for diaphragmatic hernia or pleural effusion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest Radiograph: Fine reticular granularity with ground glass appearance on both lungs; Chest Ultrasound: Not measured in provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The chest radiograph showing fine reticular granularity and a ground-glass appearance is a classic finding for Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) in a newborn, often associated with surfactant deficiency. I need to confirm your baby's gestational age and whether this was a premature birth to support this clinical picture.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
